messages:
Ethan: Quick thread 11 We need a clear mapping of runtime errors -> API surface codes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Too many teams treat any runtime mismatch as 5xx and it masks policy/regression issues.
Zara: Agreed. Proposal: classify errors into three semantic classes: TRANSIENT, CONFIG, POLICY. Map them to status codes and routing behavior.
Marta: Can you give the mapping?
Zara: Rough sketch:
- TRANSIENT -> 5xx (retryable by client / or hedging)
- CONFIG -> 4xx (route/controller misconfiguration; non-retry)
- POLICY -> 4xx/403 (customer or infra policy; do not auto-fallback unless explicitly allowed)
Ethan: How does this apply when a private sidecar is missing a capability but route fallback exists?
Ken: If route has documented fallback and customer isn't in strict_mode, we should return success (using fallback) and set response header `X-Routing-Fallback: <reason>` plus metric `routing.fallback=<reason>`. If strict_mode, return 403 (POLICY) or 422 (CONFIG) depending on why it's blocked.
Marta: We also need to avoid double-billing when hedging or fallback triggers duplicate backend work. Billing note: server-side duplicates should be de-duped by an idempotency token, billing layer must honor dedupe-window.
Ethan: Observability requirements: trace tags `error.class=TRANSIENT|CONFIG|POLICY` and `runtime.mode=hosted|dedicated|private`. Dashboards should allow pivoting by those.
Zara: Edge case: quantized variant served by private node passes functional tests but has higher hallucination rate. That's a quality regression, not a runtime error. Should be surfaced by Quality alerts and treated separately from error mapping.
Ken: For upgrades: when a node flips to a new capability, any first N failures from that node should be attributed as STAGING_ERRORS and not immediately mark the cluster as unhealthy. We need a staging bucket and alert threshold.
Marta: Testing plan: simulate private node with missing HSM & a route that prefers hosted. Expect: hosted chosen, but private candidate gets metric increment; if hosted overloaded, fallback chosen, response includes header + metric. If strict_mode true -> 403 and no fallback.
Ethan: API semantics: please document exact header names: `X-Routing-Fallback`, `X-Routing-Reason`, and `X-Routing-Mode`. Also add machine-readable field in JSON body `routing:{fallback:"int8_quant", reason:"capability_mismatch"}` for clients that prefer that.
Zara: Small caveat: avoid leaking sensitive policy info in bodies for enterprise customers. Body-level routing details should be opt-in via route flag `expose_routing_details`. Default only headers + metrics.
sre-bot: ops: canary infra `infra/canaries/error-map` available. Run `/deploy canary error-map` to validate mappings in canary traffic.
Ken: I'll draft a micro-RFC: error taxonomy, code mappings, header/body schema, staging bucket rules, billing dedupe note, and test checklist. Please review: Marta + Zara.
Marta: ACK. Keep it short, include examples for Hosted->Private failover, Dedicated eviction, and strict_mode behavior.
Ethan: Thanks all. If RFC ready by Wednesday we can run the canary end of week. :thumbsup:
